title: Grade 4 Social Studies — People and Change in Early America
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on colonies, historical evidence, trade, Ohio.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What is a primary source for learning about daily life in a colony?
choices: a diary written by someone living there
a new map of today's roads
a modern movie based on a rumor
a recent novel about another country

questions.question: People lived in what is now Ohio before Europeans arrived. What can surviving earthworks show?
choices: Every community was built by Europeans.
No one knew how to shape the land.
Native peoples lived only on ocean islands.
Native communities planned and built large structures.

questions.question: Which European country founded Jamestown in 1607?
choices: Spain
France
England
Portugal

questions.question: Why did waterways matter to many early settlements?
choices: All waterways could be crossed on foot.
Boats could never enter the rivers.
Boats could carry people and goods.
Water made every crop grow equally well.

questions.question: Which earlier event belongs before Jamestown on a timeline?
choices: The United States declared independence in 1776.
Ohio became a state in 1803.
Spain founded St. Augustine in 1565.
The U.S. Constitution was written in 1787.

questions.question: Who were the Powhatan peoples when Jamestown was founded?
choices: Native communities already living in the area
French traders living on the Ohio River
U.S. officials working for Congress
English settlers who built Jamestown

questions.question: What is one reason Europeans built trading posts near rivers in the Ohio Country?
choices: to prevent people from traveling by boat
to find an ocean coastline in Ohio
to plant all crops under water
to move trade goods along waterways

questions.question: How can archaeologists learn about people who left no written record at a site?
choices: read future newspaper stories
study objects and where they were found
use only a map of modern buses
make up names for all residents

questions.question: Which was true of enslaved people brought to English colonies?
choices: They chose jobs that always paid wages.
They had the same legal rights as others.
They could always quit and go home.
They were forced to work and denied freedom.

questions.question: What was one result of European settlement on Native lands?
choices: Some Native communities lost land or faced pressure to move.
All newcomers and Native communities agreed on every treaty.
Native people stopped having their own governments.
All Native nations chose to move at the same time.

questions.question: What might historians learn from a colonial shop's account book?
choices: the age of every road in the colony
the owner's thoughts on every customer
the flavor of each meal sold nearby
which goods the shop sold and what they cost

questions.question: What might a tool found at a historic farm reveal?
choices: the exact date of every event in the colony
which crops were never grown anywhere
how some work was done
the name of every person who touched it

questions.question: Which is a source Native communities may use to pass on knowledge?
choices: oral histories shared by community members
only writing printed before 1500
only maps drawn by European settlers
only federal court lists

questions.question: Why compare a settler's letter with a Native community's account of an event?
choices: All accounts must describe precisely the same details.
Each may describe different parts or viewpoints.
If they differ, neither can be studied.
One automatically cancels the other.

questions.question: Which shows early Americans adapting to the climate where they lived?
choices: building homes to keep out winter cold
using only one house design in every climate
building a home with no roof during each storm
ignoring the need for safe shelter

questions.question: What made Atlantic trade connect faraway communities?
choices: All farms stood in one village.
Ships moved people and goods across the ocean.
The ocean always stopped trade entirely.
Colonies never bought goods from abroad.

questions.question: A timeline shows a fort was built in 1754 and rebuilt in 1765. What happened first?
choices: the fort was rebuilt
the order cannot be known
the original fort was built
both happened in 1765

questions.question: Why should you ask who made a map of early Ohio and when?
choices: A person's name makes the map exact.
The maker and date affect what the map can show.
Every old map shows all communities equally.
The date changes the distance between places.

questions.question: Which work might involve learning a trade from a skilled person?
choices: buying a printed book once
visiting a river for one hour
keeping a calendar with no job
apprenticing with a printer

questions.question: Which material best shows what the writer of a letter valued at the time?
choices: the price of a new frame for the letter
what the writer chose to describe and ask about
the color of a library shelf
the colors of a modern folder
